content: 1. Flibanserin, when coadministered with multiple weak CYP3A4 inhibitors, requires close monitoring due to the potential for increased adverse effects. 2. Suvorexant and flibanserin both enhance sedation; therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 3. The risk of sedation is heightened when flibanserin is coadministered with other central nervous system (CNS) depressants. 4. Tacrolimus increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Flibanserin increases the levels or effects of talazoparib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Talazoparib, a P-glycoprotein substrate, may have increased systemic exposure when coadministered with P-glycoprotein inhibitors. Monitor closely. 7. Tamoxifen increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Tapentadol and flibanserin both increase sedation; therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 9. Tasimelteon and flibanserin both increase sedation; therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 10. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Tecovirimat increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP2C8 and CYP2C19 inhibitor and a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if coadministered. 13. Temazepam and flibanserin both increase sedation; therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 14. Temsirolimus increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Teniposide increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Testosterone increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Testosterone topical increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Tetracycline increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. 19. Coadministration of flibanserin with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated due to the risk of severe hypotension or syncope. 20. Thiothixene increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Serotonin modulators may enhance dopamine blockade, increasing the risk of neuroleptic malignant syndrome. 22. Antipsychotics may enhance the serotonergic effects of serotonin modulators, potentially leading to serotonin syndrome. Monitor for signs of serotonin toxicity or neuroleptic malignant syndrome. 23. Ticagrelor increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. 24. Ticlopidine increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Coadministration of flibanserin with strong CYP2C19 inhibitors may increase flibanserin exposure, raising the risk of hypotension, syncope, and CNS depression. 26. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. 27. Tramadol and flibanserin both increase sedation; therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 28. Tranylcypromine increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Trazodone increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Triazolam and flibanserin both increase sedation; therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 31. Triclabendazole increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. If plasma concentrations of CYP2C19 substrates are elevated during triclabendazole use, recheck plasma concentrations after discontinuation of triclabendazole. 33. Trifluoperazine increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 34. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 35. Valproic acid increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Venetoclax levels or effects are increased by flibanserin via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 50% and monitor for toxicities. 37. Verapamil increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. 38. Vinblastine increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Vincristine increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Vincristine liposomal increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Vinorelbine increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. 43. Zafirlukast increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Zaleplon and flibanserin both increase sedation; therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 45. Zileuton increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. 46. Ziprasidone increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Zolpidem and flibanserin both increase sedation; therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 48. Zuranolone and flibanserin may synergistically increase CNS depressant effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 49. Alcohol ingestion close to flibanserin administration increases the risk of severe hypotension and syncope. Avoid alcohol until the following day after taking flibanserin. 50. Flibanserin is contraindicated in patients with hepatic impairment due to significantly increased drug concentrations, which can lead to hypotension and syncope. 51. Malignant mammary tumors were observed in female mice at exposures 3 to 10 times the recommended clinical dose. The clinical significance of this finding is unknown. 52. There are no adequate studies in pregnant women to determine drug-associated risks. 53. It is unknown if flibanserin is distributed in human breast milk, but it is excreted in rat milk. Breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment due to the potential for serious adverse reactions in the infant. 54. Flibanserin should be taken at bedtime to reduce the risk of hypotension, syncope, and CNS depression. 55. Alcohol ingestion within 2 hours of flibanserin administration is contraindicated due to the risk of severe hypotension and syncope. 56. If alcohol is consumed in the evening, patients should wait at least 2 hours before taking flibanserin at bedtime or skip the dose entirely. 57. If a dose is missed, take the next dose at bedtime the following day. Do not double the dose. 58. Flibanserin is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4 and, to a lesser extent, by CYP2C19. Poor CYP2C19 metabolizers have increased drug exposure and a higher risk of adverse effects. 59. The frequency of poor CYP2C19 metabolizers is approximately 2–5% among Whites and Blacks and 2–15% among Asians. 60. Food increases the extent of flibanserin absorption and slows the rate of absorption. 61. Flibanserin is 98% protein-bound, primarily to albumin. 62. The half-life of flibanserin is approximately 11 hours, with excretion primarily via feces (51%) and urine (44%).
